stem: A neonate at 38 weeks gestation is delivered vaginally following an uncomplicated pregnancy.  Immediately after delivery, the neonate experiences respiratory distress.  Examination shows cyanosis, tachypnea, and poor perfusion.  The patient is urgently intubated, and mechanical ventilation is initiated.  A nasogastric tube is also inserted.  On auscultation, asymmetric aeration with decreased left-sided breath sounds is noted.  The abdomen is scaphoid.  A chest x-ray is shown in the exhibit.  Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's respiratory distress?​‌​‌​‌​​​​​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌​​​​​‌​​‌​‌​‌‌​‌​‌‌​​​​​​​‌​​‌​‌​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌​‌‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​​‌​​​‌​​‌‌​​​‌​​‌​‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​​​​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​​​​‌​​‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌​​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌​​‌‌​​​​​​‌​​‌​‌​​​​​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌​‌​‌​​​‌​​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​​‌​‌​​​‌​​​​​‌‌‌​​‌

options.label: A
options.text: Acute loss of negative pressure between visceral and parietal pleurae

explanation:
This neonate has respiratory distress with asymmetric breath sounds and a scaphoid abdomen, findings concerning for congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH).  This condition develops in the first trimester due to incomplete fusion of the pleuroperitoneal folds, which permits herniation of abdominal contents into the thoracic cavity (most commonly the left side).  Compression of the developing lung results in pulmonary hypoplasia, or underdevelopment of lung tissue.

Neonates typically develop respiratory distress (eg, tachypnea, retractions) within hours of birth and decreased unilateral breath sounds; a scaphoid abdomen from superiorly shifted abdominal viscera is common.  Classic chest x-ray findings include thoracic bowel loops with minimal or absent lung markings on the affected side; however, in the immediate postnatal period, the affected hemithorax may be partially opacified on x-ray (ie, without air-filled bowel loops) because distal bowel gas is not yet present.

Other characteristic x-ray findings include an indistinct hemidiaphragm with displacement of mediastinal structures (eg, heart), as in this patient.  In addition, the distal end of a feeding tube may be seen within the thorax instead of the abdomen.

(Choice A)  Pneumothorax is characterized by acute loss of negative pressure between the visceral and parietal pleurae (ie, intrapleural space), causing lung collapse with asymmetric breath sounds.  Although a mediastinal shift can also be seen on imaging, a visceral pleural edge with absent distal lung markings would be expected, and a scaphoid abdomen would not be seen.  Although CDH causes chronic changes in intrathoracic pressure due to mass effect, an acute loss of negative intrapleural pressure would not occur.

(Choices B and D)  Pulmonary surfactant deficiency occurs in premature, not term, neonates and causes respiratory distress syndrome (RDS).  X-ray reveals ground-glass opacities and air bronchograms.  RDS can be complicated by bronchopulmonary dysplasia, which is characterized by the dilation of airspaces with bronchiolar metaplasia.  Patients with CDH may also develop bronchopulmonary dysplasia, but this is a late complication (age >30 days).

(Choice C)  Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure measures left atrial pressure and usually estimates left ventricular end-diastolic pressure.  It is increased in certain left-sided congenital heart diseases (eg, aortic stenosis).  Poor perfusion would be expected, but a scaphoid abdomen and abnormally placed feeding tube would not be seen.

Educational objective:Congenital diaphragmatic hernia (herniation of abdominal contents into the thorax) causes pulmonary hypoplasia from lung compression.  Neonates have respiratory distress and a scaphoid abdomen after birth.  X-ray findings include thoracic bowel loops with displaced mediastinal structures; the distal end of a feeding tube may also be seen within the thorax.​‌​‌​‌​​​​​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌​​​​​‌​​‌​‌​‌‌​‌​‌‌​​​​​​​‌​​‌​‌​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌​‌‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​​‌​​​‌​​‌‌​​​‌​​‌​‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​​​​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​​​​‌​​‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌​​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌​​‌‌​​​​​​‌​​‌​‌​​​​​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌​‌​‌​​​‌​​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​​‌​‌​​​‌​​​​​‌‌‌​​‌
